name: aq_project_status
description: Get an overview of the open AnimaQuill project: its name, frame rate, picture formats and languages, its timelines with their length and number of tracks and clips, its scenes, sounds, assets and shared code files, whether you may change it, and how many problems it has. Call it at the start of a task, and again when a result says the project was reopened. It does not list clips or keyframes: use aq_timeline_read for the clips of a timeline and aq_object_read for every field of an object. Lists stop at 30 entries; use aq_search to find the rest. Like every result, it starts with the project revision, which you never need to pass back yourself.

name: aq_timeline_read
description: List what is on one timeline, one compact line per clip sorted by start: its id, name, track, start..end in seconds, what it shows (asset=, scene=, sound=, color=, text=), the transitions at its edges, its effects, and how many properties it sets and how many of them are animated. The result also lists the sections the timeline is made of, its tracks from the back of the picture forward, joins (transitions between two clips that touch) and markers. Narrow it with from and to (seconds) and tracks, and page through long timelines with cursor. Use it to find the clips you are about to change and their ids; to read every field, keyframe and effect parameter of a clip, use aq_object_read. Without timeline it reads the first timeline of the project.

timeline.description: Timeline id, as aq_project_status lists it. Without it, the first timeline of the project.

from.description: Only clips that end after this moment. Seconds as a string, such as "12.5".

to.description: Only clips that start before this moment. Seconds as a string, such as "12.5".

tracks.description: Only clips on these tracks, by track id.

limit.description: How many clips at most, 1 to 500; 200 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.

name: aq_object_read
description: Read objects of the project by id, with every field as the project format writes it: clips with their source, transitions, effects, properties and keyframes; tracks, sections, joins, markers, scenes, sounds, assets, timelines, or "project" for the project settings. The JSON you get is the same shape that aq_edit operations take, so copy from it rather than guessing. Pass fields (dotted paths such as "properties.transform.x" or "effects") to read only those. For a clip that shows a scene it also lists the properties the scene describes, with their type, unit, range and default: use these paths with property.edit. Clip ids are unique only within a timeline; pass timeline when several timelines have the same id. Read up to 20 objects in one call; with response_format "concise" you get one line per object and a summary of its top-level fields instead of the full JSON.

ids.description: Ids of clips, tracks, sections, joins, markers, scenes, sounds, assets or timelines, or "project", 1 to 20.

timeline.description: Timeline id, for ids that several timelines have.

fields.description: Dotted paths to read only these fields, such as "start", "properties.transform.x" or "effects".

response_format.description: "detailed" (the default) gives every field as JSON; "concise" one line per object and its top-level fields.

name: aq_search
description: Find objects in the project by id, name, kind or text, when you know what you are looking for but not where it is: clips that show a given asset or scene, a track by name, markers, scenes, sounds, assets, files by path, or text inside the code of scenes and sounds (kind "text", which answers with path:line and the line). Matching ignores case and finds the query anywhere in the id, name, path or source. Without query it lists everything of the given kinds. Results are compact lines with ids you can use in other tools.

query.description: Text to find, any case, in ids, names, paths, sources, or the text of code files (kind text).

kinds.description: Only these kinds of objects; every kind but text by default.

timeline.description: Only objects of this timeline, by its id.

limit.description: How many results at most, 1 to 200; 50 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.

name: aq_file_read
description: Read a code file of the project: the HTML, CSS and JavaScript of a scene (under scenes/<id>/), the code of a sound (under sounds/<id>/), or shared code (under code/). Lines come numbered as "   12→text"; the numbers are not part of the file, so leave them out when you copy text into aq_file_edit. Long files come in parts: pass offset (the first line) and limit (how many lines). Read all of a file before you replace it with aq_file_write, which requires it, and before you edit it, so that you copy its exact text. Project settings, timelines, scenes' manifests and assets are not files you read here: use aq_object_read for them.

path.description: Path of a code file, such as "scenes/title/index.html", as aq_project_status or aq_search lists it.

offset.description: The first line to read, from 1; 1 by default.

limit.description: How many lines at most, 1 to 2000; 2000 by default.

name: aq_selection_read
description: See what the user is pointing at in the editor: the timeline they are on, the playhead time, the current version, the selected clips (ids and one line each) and the selected transition. The editor records this as each message of the user is sent. Call it when the user says "this", "here", "these clips" or "now": with at "sent" for what they pointed at as they sent a message (messages_back counts back from the latest message, 0 by default), with at "now" for what they point at right now. It only gives what the user chose to share with you; read the full objects with aq_object_read.

at.description: "sent": as a message of the user was sent, see messages_back. "now": as the editor is now.

messages_back.description: Only with at "sent": which message of the user, counted back from the latest: 0 (the default) is the latest, the one this task started with, 1 the one before it.

name: aq_guide
description: Read the AnimaQuill manual. It has a reference page for every operation of aq_edit (topic "ops/<operation>", such as "ops/property.edit": parameters, what it returns, its errors, examples), the project format (topics "format/…": times, ids, world coordinates, clips, transitions, effects, properties and keyframes) and how scene code talks to the editor (topics "scene-runtime/…"). Call it without arguments for the table of contents, with topic for one page, or with query to search by keywords. Look things up here instead of guessing: read the page of an operation before its first use when its parameters are not obvious, and the scene runtime pages when scene code has to work with the editor (its properties, time, assets or fonts).

topic.description: One page, such as "ops/clip.move", "format/animaquill.json" or "scene-runtime/aq"; ":2" after it for its next part. Without topic and query, the table of contents.

query.description: Words to look for in titles and pages; it gives up to 10 topics, each with a line of what it says.

name: aq_edit
description:
Change the open project with a batch of operations — the same operations the editor's own commands use. All operations of one call succeed together or nothing is written, and the batch is one step the user can undo. Operations run in order, so a later one can refer to an object an earlier one created: give new objects ids of your own, such as "clip_title2", and use them in the same batch. Use it for everything about timelines, sections, tracks, clips, transitions, joins, effects, properties and keyframes, markers, scenes, sounds and assets. Do not use it for the text of code files: change code with aq_file_edit or aq_file_write. To create a scene or a sound, use scene.add or sound.add with its files in the same operation. Times are strings in seconds, such as "12.5" or "1001/30000". Positions and sizes are in world units, with the origin at the center of the picture. Ids come from the reading tools; never invent ids of existing objects. Before a batch that deletes several objects, send it with dry_run: true first to see everything it would remove, including what uses those objects. If the user changed something you are about to change after you last read it, the call fails with conflict and writes nothing: read it again, then decide. A failed call says which operation failed, why, the correct shape and an example. The result lists the objects that changed, the ids of new objects, and the problems this batch introduced or resolved — fix the problems you introduced. Write summary as one short sentence that tells the user what the batch does, without your reasoning. Operations (every parameter, result and more examples: aq_guide topic "ops/"): project.rename {name} — rename the project project.setFrameRate {fps} — set the frame rate the timeline counts frames by project.setDescription {description} — set the description of the project project.setCredits {credits:[{role, name}]} — set the credits of the project project.setFormats {formats:[{id, name, width, height, fps, safeArea?}]} — set the picture formats, the first the master project.setLanguages {languages:[{id, name, font?}]} — set the languages, the first the master project.setCover {cover} — set the moment the cover of the project shows asset.update {asset, changes:{name?, tags?:[string]}} — rename an asset or change its tags asset.remove {asset, withUses?} — remove an asset, and with withUses the clips that use it scene.add {id?, manifest, files:object} — create a scene (HTML, CSS and JavaScript that draw a picture) with its files scene.update {scene, changes:object, clear?:["description"|"params"|"presets"|"tags"]} — change the manifest of a scene: name, entry, params, presets scene.remove {scene, withUses?} — remove a scene and its files, and with withUses the clips that use it sound.add {id?, manifest, files:object} — create a sound made by code, with its files sound.update {sound, changes:object, clear?:["description"|"params"|"outputs"|"tags"]} — change the manifest of a sound: name, entry, params, outputs sound.remove {sound, withUses?} — remove a sound and its files, and with withUses the clips that use it source.replace {kind, from, to} — make every clip that uses an asset, scene or sound use another one of the same kind clip.add {timeline, track, name?, start, duration, source, offset?, loop?, enter?, exit?, hidden?, draft?, link?, sectionFit?, properties?:object, effects?:[{id, type, enabled?, start?, end?}], id?, overlap?, rippleTracks?:[string]} — put a clip on a track: an asset, a scene, a sound, a color or a caption clip.remove {timeline, clips:[string], ripple?, rippleTracks?:[string]} — remove clips; with ripple, move what follows back into their place clip.update {timeline, clip, changes:{name?, source?, offset?, loop?, hidden?, draft?, link?, sectionFit?}, clear?:["name"|"offset"|"loop"|"hidden"|"draft"|"link"|"sectionFit"]} — change the name, source, offset, loop, hidden, draft, link or section fit of a clip clip.move {timeline, clips:[{clip, start?, track?}], overlap?, rippleTracks?:[string]} — move clips to other starts or tracks, in one step clip.trim {timeline, clip, start?, end?, together?:[string], ripple?, rippleTracks?:[string]} — move the start or end of a clip; what it shows stays in place; with ripple, what follows moves along clip.slip {timeline, clips:[string], by} — slip clips: keep where they are and how long, and show what is later or earlier in them clip.slide {timeline, clips:[string], by} — slide clips; the clips right next to them get longer and shorter to make up clip.roll {timeline, edges:[{clip, edge}], at} — move the cut between two clips; one gets longer, the other shorter, together as long clip.split {timeline, clip, at, piece?, keep?:[string]} — cut a clip in two at a moment of the timeline clip.link {timeline, clips:[string]} — link clips into a group, like the picture and sound of a video clip.unlink {timeline, clips:[string]} — take clips out of their linked groups file.remove {path} — remove a code file that is no entry file.rename {from, to} — rename or move a code file timeline.rename {timeline, name} — rename a timeline timeline.setBackground {timeline, background} — set the background color of a timeline timeline.setDefault {timeline} — make a timeline open first section.add {timeline, id?, duration, name?, before?} — add a section to a timeline, which makes it longer section.update {timeline, section, duration?, name?, clear?:["name"]} — change the duration or name of a section section.split {timeline, at, id?, name?} — split a section in two at a moment; the length stays section.moveBoundary {timeline, section, at} — move the boundary after a section; the length stays section.remove {timeline, section} — remove a section; its time goes to the one before it timeline.closeGap {timeline, ranges:[{from, to}], rippleTracks?:[string]} — take empty stretches out of a timeline; what follows moves back timeline.openGap {timeline, at, duration, rippleTracks?:[string]} — put empty time into a timeline; what follows moves on timeline.removeRange {timeline, from, to, tracks?:[string], ripple?} — take away what is on tracks between two moments; with ripple, close that time too track.add {timeline, id?, kind, name?, before?} — add a video, audio or caption track track.update {timeline, track, changes:{name?, locked?, group?, hidden?, muted?, solo?, role?}} — change the name, hidden, muted, solo, locked, group or role of a track track.move {timeline, track, before?} — move a track before another one, or last track.remove {timeline, track} — remove a track with all its clips clip.setTransition {timeline, clip, enter?, exit?} — put a transition at the start (enter) or end (exit) of a clip, or take it away with null join.add {type?, transition?, library?, resource?, duration?, curve?, values?:object, timeline, id?, from, to, align?} — put a transition on the cut between two clips that touch join.update {timeline, join, changes:{type?, transition?, library?, resource?, duration?, curve?, values?, align?}} — change the type, duration, align, curve or values of a join join.remove {timeline, joins:[string]} — remove joins effect.add {timeline, clip, id?, type, enabled?, index?, values?:object, start?, end?} — put an effect on a clip, with the values of its parameters effect.remove {timeline, clip, effects:[string]} — take effects off a clip effect.move {timeline, clip, effect, index} — move an effect in the list of its clip, which changes what it works on effect.update {timeline, clip, effect, enabled?, start?, end?} — turn an effect on or off, or change when it works property.edit {timeline, edits:[PropertyEdit]} — set properties of clips and their keyframes, in one step property.rename {timeline, renames:[PropertyRename]} — give properties of a clip another path, with their keyframes, after code renamed what they are about marker.add {timeline, id?, time, name?, note?, color?, duration?} — add a marker to a timeline marker.update {timeline, marker, changes:{time?, name?, note?, color?, duration?}, clear?:["name"|"note"|"color"|"duration"]} — change the time, name, note, color or duration of a marker marker.remove {timeline, marker} — remove a marker Examples of operations (illustrative; their ids come from a sample project, so use the ids name: aq_file_edit
description: Change part of a code file by replacing exact text: for each edit, old_text must appear exactly once in the file as it is now (copy it from aq_file_read without the line numbers, with enough surrounding lines to be unique), and it is replaced with new_text. Set replace_all to replace every occurrence instead. All edits of one call are applied in order and succeed together, or nothing is written. This is the way to change scene, sound and shared code; it does not need the file's revision, so the user may edit other parts of the same file meanwhile. If old_text is not found, the user may have just changed that part: read the file again. The result shows the changed lines and a syntax check. To create a file or rewrite most of one, use aq_file_write.

path.description: Path of the code file, such as "scenes/title/index.html".

old_text.description: Text of the file as it is now, exactly, without the line numbers of aq_file_read; enough of it to be found once.

replace_all.description: true replaces every place old_text is found, at least one.

request_id.description: Any string of yours: a call sent again with the same one is not run again and gets the same result.

name: aq_file_write
description: Create a code file, or replace all of one: a new file of a scene, sound or shared code, or a rewrite of most of a file. Paths go under scenes/<scene id>/, sounds/<sound id>/ or code/; the scene or sound must exist (create it with scene.add or sound.add in aq_edit, which takes its first files too). To replace an existing file you must have read all its lines with aq_file_read in this conversation, and the call fails with file-changed if somebody changed it since: read it again, then write. For small changes use aq_file_edit, which keeps the user's edits elsewhere in the file. The result includes a syntax check.

path.description: Path of the file, under scenes/<scene id>/, sounds/<sound id>/ or code/, such as "code/ease.js".

base_revision.description: Hardly ever needed: a revision from an earlier result, to also refuse the write if the file changed since then. The file still has to be read first.

request_id.description: Any string of yours: a call sent again with the same one is not run again and gets the same result.

name: aq_propose
description: Hand a decision to the user and stop this turn to wait for it. Use kind "question" when you cannot go on without the user's choice — which of two clips they meant, which of a few styles they want, whether to replace or keep something — and give 2 to 6 short, concrete options; the user can also answer in their own words. Do not ask about what you can find out by reading the project, and ask one question at a time. Use kind "plan" when the user asked for a plan first: give the steps with their times, and the user changes or accepts it. After calling it, end your turn without further tools: the answer arrives as the user's next message.

kind.description: "question": a choice for the user to make. "plan": the plan of the work, before any change.

question.description: The question, in one sentence, in the language of the user.

label.description: A short answer the user can pick.

detail.description: What picking it means, in a few words.

allow_other.description: false when the user must pick one of the options; by default they can also answer in their own words.

title.description: The plan in a few words, in the language of the user.

steps.description: The steps of the plan, in order, 1 to 20.

text.description: What the step does, in one line.

from.description: Where it starts, seconds as a string such as "4".

to.description: Where it ends, seconds as a string.

length.description: How long the result is, seconds as a string.

style.description: The look and feel, in a few words.

name: aq_render_frames
description:
Renders frames of a timeline as the export renders them. The pictures come first in the result, and after them what is on each frame: every clip that shows, back to front, with its id and name, what it shows, its box in world units, the share of the picture it covers, its opacity, how far it goes past the edges of the picture, whether its media is cut to its box, and which small clips overlap; and the text elements of HTML scenes with their text and box. A frame that cannot be rendered whole, as when the file of an asset is not on this computer or a scene does not run, gives an error with the reason, and no picture: a picture is only ever what the export would render.

times gives a picture of each moment. range with count is an overview: count frames evenly spread over the range in one picture, each with its time printed on it. region is a part of the picture rendered at the full size of a picture: scenes are laid out again at that resolution, so their text stays sharp, while videos and images are scaled up. annotate draws on the picture a box with the id and name of each clip (true) or of the clips given, red where one goes past an edge. compare gives, for each time, the frame before, the frame now and a picture where the changed pixels are red, with the share of pixels that changed and the box around them: "task_start" is the project as this task started, and a revision is the project as an earlier result of this conversation started (its rev line). size small, medium or large is 512, 1024 or 1568 pixels on the longer side; a 1024×576 picture costs about 790 tokens; without size, the size the user set. Each frame is the one the export renders at that moment. A model that cannot see pictures gets the text only. Rendering waits while the user plays or exports, and while the editor page is in the background, as the browser draws nothing then; that wait is part of the call and no failure.

times.description: Moments to render, 1 to 8, seconds as strings such as "12.5"; each gives a picture. Not with range.

range.description: An overview: {"from": "0", "to": "30"}, seconds as strings; count frames evenly spread from from, all in one picture. Not with times, region or compare.

count.description: How many frames an overview has, 2 to 24; 12 by default. Only with range.

timeline.description: Timeline id, as aq_project_status lists it. Without it, the first timeline of the project.

version.description: Picture format id, as aq_project_status lists it, for that version of the picture. Without it, the first format.

size.description: "small" (512 pixels on the longer side), "medium" (1024) or "large" (1568). Without it, the size the user set, medium by default.

region.description: A part of the picture to render at the full size of a picture, in world units: {"x": -960, "y": 0, "width": 960, "height": 540} is the bottom left quarter of a 1920×1080 picture; x and y are its top left corner, from the center of the picture.

annotate.description: true draws a box with the id and name of every clip on the picture; a list of clip ids draws only those, 1 to 20.

compare.description: "task_start", or a revision such as "k3x9:42" from the rev line of an earlier result of this conversation: each time is rendered as the project was then and as it is now, with what differs. At most 4 times.

name: aq_audio_analyze
description: Mixes a part of a timeline as the export mixes it and measures it: stereo at 48 kHz, with volumes and sound transitions as set; muted tracks are not heard, and only soloed tracks where a track is soloed. Nothing is played to the user. loudness gives the integrated loudness in LUFS and the loudest 3 seconds (short-term max), as ITU-R BS.1770-4 and EBU R128 measure them, the true peak in dBTP (between samples too) and the sample peak in dBFS. For orientation: online video and streaming aim at about -14 LUFS integrated with the true peak at or below -1 dBTP; broadcast (EBU R128) at -23 LUFS. silence gives each stretch below -50 dBFS for 0.3 s or longer. clipping gives each place where samples stay at full scale for 3 samples or more, or go over it (the export cuts those), with how many samples. envelope gives where the sound is loudest, its attack (from 10% to 90% of its peak) and its decay (from the peak to 40 dB below it): check a short sound made by code with it. clip measures that clip alone over its time on the timeline, as if nothing else sounded. Times in the result are seconds on the timeline. A part where the file of an asset is not on this computer, or the code of a sound did not make it, gives an error with the reason and no numbers: a measure is only ever of what the export would give.

range.description: The part to measure: {"from": "0", "to": "30"}, seconds as strings, at most 600 seconds long. Without it, the whole timeline, or the time of clip on it.

timeline.description: Timeline id, as aq_project_status lists it. Without it, the first timeline of the project.

version.description: Picture format id, as aq_project_status lists it; the sound of every format is the same today. Without it, the first format.

clip.description: A clip id: measures only that clip, as if nothing else sounded, such as a sound made by code.

what.description: Which measures: "loudness", "silence", "clipping", "envelope". By default loudness, silence and clipping; with clip, loudness, clipping and envelope.

name: aq_check_run
description: Check the project and list its problems: files that do not fit the project format, references to things that are missing, values that do not fit what a scene describes, errors that scene and sound code threw when the editor ran it, and things this editor version does not do yet (they will not appear in the preview or the export). Run it after changing code, and before you tell the user you are done; fix the problems you caused and mention the others. Problems with a fix line are fixed by sending that operation to aq_edit. Runtime errors only come from code the editor has run, which happens shortly after a change; aq_edit results already include the problems that come from the project data alone.

checks.description: "format": whether every document fits the project format; "problems": all problems the editor knows of. Both by default.

subject.description: Only problems of this object id or file path.

limit.description: How many problems at most, 1 to 500; 100 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.
